topic: Among patients with endometrial cancer, is low-volume sentinel-node metastasis associated with recurrence compared with pathologically node-negative status?

pico.population: Patients with surgically staged endometrial cancer

targets.comparison: Low-volume sentinel-node metastasis (isolated tumor cells or micrometastasis) versus pathologically node-negative status
targets.population_or_subgroup: Patients with surgically staged endometrial cancer

timepoint_policy.rule: Capture any recurrence during each study's stated follow-up; preserve follow-up duration rather than imputing a common timepoint.

extraction_notes: Extract source counts and denominators, including the explicitly permitted disjoint-stratum aggregation; preserve cohort, outcome, follow-up and derivation provenance. Do not calculate effects.
source_constraints: For the same cohort, outcome and follow-up, explicitly disjoint ITC and micrometastasis strata may be combined by summing their reported integer events and denominators once. Record each original stratum and the addition in source_quote; never count a combined row and its component rows as independent studies.

An exhaustive source recurrence roster may support an exact count by nodal status only when every relevant record has an unambiguous group assignment and the matching denominators are reported. State the roster and counting basis; otherwise leave the count unresolved.

Do not infer recurrence counts from percentages, Kaplan-Meier survival, hazard ratios, disease-free counts or review tables. Preserve incomplete arm counts and their missing fields in unresolved_items; never fill missing counts with zero.
Preserve true zero-event arms as zero. Continuity correction and RR calculation belong to the downstream calculator.
